findings.title: The four-value work-purpose vocabulary is a bare string literal list duplicated across three source files rather than one shared constant
findings.failure_scenario: The same four-member set is re-typed by hand in apps/web/components/work/accounting-work-list.tsx's KNOWN_PURPOSE_LABELS Set and apps/web/components/work/work-list-filters.tsx's KNOWN_PURPOSES array, with no shared source of truth. A fifth purpose value added to the database column's CHECK in a future ticket could be added to one or two of the three lists and missed in the third, degrading silently to a raw DB token or an 'A kind not in this list' filter entry rather than a compile error.
findings.required_fix: Not required of this ticket: the pattern (three independent lists) pre-dates #984 -- the ticket only appended 'opening_balance' consistently to each existing list, exactly as its own predecessor values were already split three ways. The repo already carries a standing structural guard for exactly this drift (apps/web/lib/work/staff-expense-claim.test.ts's `purpose.four` cross-surface census, re-derived by this same diff), so a future drift is caught by an existing test rather than silently. Worth a follow-up refactor (extract one shared `WORK_PURPOSES` tuple the three call sites derive from) but out of scope for this lane and not a regression it introduced.

findings.title: None of the five per-ticket reports document running the CI-flagged lint variant RIG.md's wave-2 addendum explicitly requires before reporting
findings.hunk:
- CI sets `CI=true` and `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, and some CLIs here refuse ceremony acts under CI
  (`--retire`, `--update`, `--lock-deployed`). ... Before you report,
  run the lint chain once more as the runner sees it: `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint`
  (wave 1 shipped a cell that was green on the rig and red on the runner, PR #1025).
findings.failure_scenario: None of reports/wave2-lane01-ticket1014.md, ticket868.md, ticket906.md, ticket914.md or ticket984.md mentions `CI=true` or `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` anywhere -- every one only reports the plain `pnpm lint`. Running the CI-flagged variant myself found a real failure: `freeze-lint selftest: FAIL -- 1 case(s) failed` on the case '(L05-STD-02 fix round) --ruling followed by another flag ... not swallowed as the literal ruling text', because under CI the tool now refuses `--retire` itself before it reaches the ruling-parsing branch the selftest is probing. This is NOT this lane's defect: `scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs` and `scripts/check-frozen-workflows.selftest.mjs` are both byte-identical between the fixed point and HEAD (empty `git diff`), and packages/runtime is untouched by this lane's whole diff -- so the failure is a pre-existing, wave-2-base residue in the same class as the `document-kind-dialog.tsx` typecheck red all five reports already disclose. But because the gate was never run, none of the five reports could have disclosed it, and an integrator relying on the reports' own 'pnpm lint: exit 0' line alone would not learn that the CI runner will fail differently from the rig -- exactly the PR #1025 lesson RIG.md cites this rule to prevent.
findings.required_fix: No code fix owed by this lane (the failing selftest is outside every ticket's files). The fix is procedural: a future lane report in this wave should run and record `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint` per RIG.md, and the integrator should track scripts/check-frozen-workflows.selftest.mjs's CI-only red as a known wave-2-base residue (alongside document-kind-dialog.tsx) rather than something any single lane needs to fix.

summary: Five tickets (#1014, #868, #906, #914, #984), fifteen commits, five new migrations (0235-0239), all independently re-verified on the lane rig: every re-run test file (25 individual cells across opening-balance-evidence-link, correction-client-rung-order, subledger-hook-caller-roster, journal-basis-zero-total-unreachable and opening-balance-work) passed exactly as each report claimed, and operation-census/rig-isolation passed with only the one RIG.md-documented reset-gated skip. Every migration follows house law: a redo-tolerant prestate measuring live shas/ACLs/CHECK text before writing, `set role clara_fn_owner`/`reset role` around any recut body, a tail that re-derives every claim from the catalog rather than trusting the prestate, a preintegration gate module registered at the sorted position, and a rig-meta.mjs cohort entry (or an explicit, precedented statement of why none is owed) for every new relation or grant. #1014's new table is RLS-enabled-and-forced with exactly one owner policy and zero application-role grants; #984's new internal function has EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC and is reachable only from the two already-audited human doors. No applied migration, PRD, ARCHITECTURE or frozen-workflow file was touched. TDD discipline holds at the commit level (test and implementation land together, vertical-slice by vertical-slice, with documented red-for-the-right-reason and vacuity-control evidence in every report) and every seam tested is either a real human door driven as a real session or a structural/catalog census the work order's own rule 4 carve-out covers, declared as such up front. Two non-blocking findings: a pre-existing (not this lane's) three-way duplication of the work-purpose value list, already guarded by an existing cross-surface census test (note); and none of the five reports ran the CI-flagged `pnpm lint` variant RIG.md's wave-2 addendum explicitly requires, which independently surfaced one real but pre-existing (wave-2-base, files this lane never touched) freeze-lint selftest failure that the reports' plain 'pnpm lint: exit 0' line does not disclose (minor, procedural).
